mainTopic: The כוי and partial-שה rules, the status of forest goats for the מזבח, and whether the משנה of אותו ואת בנו follows רבי שמעון.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the argument between רבנן and רבי אליעזר: does the word שה include an animal that is only partly a שה? רב פפא explains that both sides are unsure whether the father's species counts. So for כסוי הדם and מתנות, the case must be a כוי from a deer father and a goat mother. For אותו ואת בנו, both kinds of כוי work: with a goat father the argument is over a plain איסור, and with a deer father it is over מלקות. The גמרא then brings other views of what a כוי is: its own creature of undecided status, a wild ram, a goat-deer cross, or a בהמה, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says. Next, רב המנונא rules that forest goats may be brought on the מזבח because they are not on the תורה's list of wild animals. The גמרא challenges this: maybe they are the listed אקו, תאו or זמר, and אמימר even permitted their fat. A second version of the same discussion, based on the argument about שור הבר, meets the same challenges. Finally, רבי אושעיא says the whole משנה of כיצד השוחט does not follow רבי שמעון. The proof, built on his rule that an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The core disagreement: does 'partly a sheep' count?
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that the word שה includes even an animal that is only partly a שה. רבי אליעזר holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about the word 'sheep' and whether it includes even something that is only partly a sheep. רבנן hold that 'sheep' includes even a partial sheep. רבי אליעזר holds that 'sheep' means a full sheep, not a partial one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question of what רבנן and רבי אליעזר are really arguing about. It points to how each side reads the word שה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is not about the facts of the animal. It is about how to read the פסוק. For רבנן, any domesticated part is enough to be called שה. For רבי אליעזר, the animal must be completely domesticated, so a mixed animal is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheep or goat; the word the פסוק uses for a domesticated animal
Partly a שה, such as an animal with one domesticated parent
They hold / he holds (their opinion or reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי אליעזר says a mixed animal is a wild animal. He only says it does not get the rules of a שה, because it is not fully a שה.

phrases.english: Concerning 'sheep' — and whether it includes even part of a sheep.
The Rabbis hold: 'sheep' — even partly a sheep;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: ״שֶׂה״ – וְלֹא מִקְצָת שֶׂה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Eliezer holds: 'sheep' — but not partly a sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: ״שֶׂה״ – וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת שֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question (from before this section) about what the two sides argue about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the מחלוקת between רבנן and רבי אליעזר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether the word שה includes an animal that is only partly a שה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the cases only work with a deer and a female goat
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes that the rules of כסוי הדם and מתנות for a כוי can only be explained when it comes from a male צבי that mated with a female goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: therefore, for covering the blood and for the priestly gifts, you can only find the case in a deer that mated with a female goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a practical conclusion from the מחלוקת. He limits which kind of כוי the rules about covering blood and giving gifts can be talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules being explained are covering the כוי's blood out of doubt, and the argument over giving מתנות from it. Both only make sense when the mother is a domesticated goat and the father is a wild צבי. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore; a conclusion drawn from what was just said
Covering the blood after שחיטה, required for a wild animal or a bird
The gifts given to a כהן from a domesticated animal (the foreleg, cheeks and stomach)
You cannot find it except in; the case only works when
A male deer that mated with a female goat

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us exactly which כוי the rulings about blood and gifts are talking about. That keeps the opinions consistent with each other.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says: Therefore,
with regard to covering the blood and the priestly gifts,
phrases.notes: These are the rules for a כוי, a creature whose status as wild or domesticated is in doubt.

phrases.english: you do not find it except
with a deer that mated with a female goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הִלְכָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מחלוקת from step 1 to pin down the case of the כוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The laws of כסוי הדם and מתנות for a כוי apply only to one born from a male צבי and a female goat.

steps.title: Both sides are unsure whether the father counts
steps.stepSummary: The reason for רב פפא's conclusion: both רבנן and רבי אליעזר are in doubt whether we take the father's side into account.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because both רבנן and רבי אליעזר are unsure whether we are concerned about the father's seed or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first half of the reason behind רב פפא's ruling. On this point both sides agree: they are unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father's side counts, a כוי from a צבי father is partly wild. If the father's side does not count, the animal follows its domesticated mother completely. Because nobody knows which is true, the blood is covered out of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: They are in doubt about it
We take the father's seed into account (whether the father's species matters)

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the point they argue about. Both רבנן and רבי אליעזר share this same doubt.

phrases.english: For both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Eliezer,
it is uncertain to them

phrases.aramaic: אִי חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְזֶרַע הָאָב אוֹ לָא.
phrases.english: whether we are concerned with the father's seed or not.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵין לְרַבָּנַן, וּבֵין לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, מְסַפְּקָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב פפא's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides are in doubt whether the father's species is taken into account.

steps.title: Their real argument is only about 'partly a sheep'
steps.stepSummary: The only thing רבנן and רבי אליעזר argue about is whether 'partly a שה' counts as a שה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they disagree about 'sheep' and whether it includes even part of a sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב פפא's explanation. Their actual disagreement is the reading of שה from step 1, now applied to the כוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כוי has a domesticated mother, so it is at least partly a שה. For רבנן that is enough, so the כהן's מתנות are given from it. For רבי אליעזר it is not enough, so he exempts it. Covering the blood out of doubt fits the view of רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: For a כוי born from a male צבי and a female goat, both sides are unsure whether the father counts. They argue only over whether 'partly a שה' is a שה: yes for רבנן, so מתנות are given; no for רבי אליעזר, so it is exempt.

phrases.english: And they disagree
about 'sheep — and even part of a sheep.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא מִיפַּלְגִי בְּ״שֶׂה וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת שֶׂה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning begun in step 3 by naming the true point of disagreement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת over the כוי is only whether 'partly a שה' counts as a שה. The doubt about the father's seed is shared by both sides.

steps.title: For אותו ואת בנו, both kinds of כוי work
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that the argument about אותו ואת בנו can be about either kind of כוי: a goat father with a deer mother, or a deer father with a goat mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it comes to אותו ואת בנו, you can find the case either with a male goat that mated with a female deer, or with a male deer that mated with a female goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves from כסוי הדם and מתנות to a new topic, אותו ואת בנו. He says this topic works for both kinds of כוי, and he is setting up the next two steps, which explain each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For כסוי הדם and מתנות, רב פפא said only one kind of כוי fits (deer father, goat mother). Here he says something different: for אותו ואת בנו, both kinds fit. He still has to show how each case leads to an argument, and that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור against slaughtering a mother animal and its child on the same day
You can find it, meaning there is a case where this works

phrases.english: Regarding the matter of 'it and its offspring,'
phrases.notes: This is the rule in ויקרא 22:28: don't slaughter a mother animal and its child on the same day.

phrases.english: you can find it
either with a male goat that mates with a female deer,
or with a male deer that mates with a female goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב פפא's analysis to a new halacha, אותו ואת בנו, where both kinds of כוי work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument about a כוי and אותו ואת בנו can be about either kind of כוי.

steps.title: Goat father, deer mother: an argument about a plain prohibition
steps.stepSummary: When the father is a goat and the mother is a deer, רבנן say it is אסור, because maybe the father counts, which would make it partly a שה. רבי אליעזר says that even if the father counts, partly a שה is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of a male goat with a female deer, the argument is about whether it is forbidden. רבנן hold: maybe we take the father into account, and we say 'שה, even partly a שה,' so it is forbidden. רבי אליעזר holds: even if we do take the father into account, we don't say 'even partly a שה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the first case. Here the mother is a deer, so the only 'sheep' side comes from the goat father, and it is a doubt whether the father even counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother is a deer, so without the father this animal is just a deer. If the father counts, the animal is partly a שה. Since that is only a doubt, רבנן can only say it is forbidden, not that someone gets מלקות. רבי אליעזר permits it, because even if the father counts, partly a שה is not a שה for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition, meaning it is forbidden, but here without מלקות
We take the father's side into account
Partly a שה, an animal only partly from the sheep or goat family

steps.confusionAlert: In this case the 'sheep' side comes from the father, not the mother. So without the father, this animal is a full deer. That is why רבנן only say 'maybe' and only forbid it.

phrases.english: With a male goat that mates with a female deer, the case is about a prohibition,
as the Rabbis hold:
perhaps we take the father's side into account,
and we say 'a שה, even partly a שה,' so it is forbidden.
And רבי אליעזר holds:
even if we do take the father's side into account,
we do not say 'a שה, even partly a שה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּתַיִישׁ הַבָּא עַל הַצְּבִיָּיה, וּלְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two cases introduced in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Goat father with deer mother: רבנן forbid it, because maybe the father counts and partly a שה is a שה. רבי אליעזר permits it, because partly a שה is not a שה.

steps.title: Deer father, goat mother: an argument about מלקות
steps.stepSummary: When the father is a deer and the mother is a goat, רבנן give מלקות, since either way it is at least partly a שה. רבי אליעזר says it is forbidden but there is no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of a male deer with a female goat, the argument is about מלקות. רבנן hold: even if we take the father into account, we say 'even partly a שה,' so we give him מלקות. רבי אליעזר holds: there is a prohibition, but there is no מלקות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the second case. Now the mother is a goat, so the animal is surely at least partly a שה, and the argument is about whether there is מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father doesn't count, this is a full שה. If the father does count, it is partly a שה, and רבנן say that is still a שה, so there is מלקות either way. For רבי אליעזר, if the father counts it is not a שה, so it is a doubt: forbidden, but no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes, the punishment for breaking a definite Torah prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: For אותו ואת בנו both kinds of כוי work. Goat father: רבנן forbid, רבי אליעזר permits. Deer father: רבנן give מלקות, רבי אליעזר forbids without מלקות. In both cases the real argument is only whether 'partly a שה' counts as a שה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows step 4's conclusion in action. Both sides are unsure about the father, and the only real argument is about 'partly a שה.'

phrases.english: With a male deer that mates with a female goat, the case is about lashes.
The Rabbis hold:
even if we do take the father's side into account,
we say 'a שה, even partly a שה,'
and we give him lashes.
And רבי אליעזר holds:
there is a prohibition, but there are no lashes.
phrases.notes: It is forbidden because maybe the father doesn't count and it is a full שה. Since it is only a maybe, there are no lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּצְבִי הַבָּא עַל הַתְּיָישָׁה, וּלְמַלְקוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second case from step 5, finishing רב פפא's analysis of אותו ואת בנו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deer father with goat mother: רבנן give מלקות, since it is at least partly a שה either way. רבי אליעזר forbids it but gives no מלקות, because it is only a doubt.

steps.title: Why רבי אליעזר forbids it but gives no lashes
steps.stepSummary: For a כוי from a deer father and a goat mother, רבי אליעזר holds there is an איסור, because maybe we ignore the father and it is a full שה. There are no מלקות, because maybe the father does count, and partly a שה is not a שה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a prohibition, because maybe we do not take the father into account, and then this animal is a full שה. There are no lashes, because maybe we do take the father into account. And רבי אליעזר does not say 'שה means even partly a שה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's ruling from Step 7: forbidden, but no מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on the doubt about the father's side. If the father does not count, the כוי is a full goat like its mother, so it is forbidden. If the father does count, it is only partly a שה, and רבי אליעזר holds that partly a שה is not included. Because of this doubt, it is forbidden, but there are no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes given by בית דין for breaking a Torah prohibition
We take the father's side into account
A full, complete שה (sheep or goat)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, a כוי from a goat mother is forbidden because of the doubt, but gets no מלקות, since partly a שה does not count as a שה.
steps.confusionAlert: The doubt here is NOT whether the mother is a goat. She definitely is. The doubt is only whether the deer father's side counts at all.

phrases.english: There is a prohibition,
since perhaps we are not concerned with the father's side,
phrases.notes: The father here is a deer. If we ignore him, the animal just follows its goat mother.

phrases.english: and then this is a full-fledged שה.
There are no lashes,
since perhaps we are concerned with the father's side.

phrases.aramaic: וְ״שֶׂה וַאֲפִילּוּ מִקְצָת שֶׂה״ לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: And we do not say 'שה, and even partly a שה.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's ruling in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The animal is forbidden because maybe the father does not count. There are no מלקות because maybe the father counts, and partly a שה is not a שה.

steps.title: Two views on what a כוי is
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says a כוי is its own kind of creature, and the חכמים never decided whether it is a בהמה or a חיה. רב נחמן says a כוי is a wild ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: a כוי is a creature of its own, and the חכמים did not decide whether it is a kind of domesticated animal or a kind of wild animal. רב נחמן said: a כוי is the wild ram.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. Until now it treated a כוי as a cross between a goat and a deer, and now it brings other opinions about what a כוי really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה says a כוי is not a mix at all. It is its own species, and its status as a בהמה or a חיה was simply never settled. רב נחמן gives it a clear identity: a wild ram.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status as a בהמה or a חיה is unclear
A creature of its own, a separate category

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
A koy is a creature of its own,
and the Sages did not decide about it
whether it is a species of domesticated animal
or a species of wild animal.
Rav Nachman said:
A koy is the wild ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כּוֹי – בְּרִיָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the goat-deer analysis and opens a new question about what a כוי is
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: a כוי is its own species, of undecided status. רב נחמן: a כוי is a wild ram.

steps.title: The same argument among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא already records several opinions about the כוי: a wild ram, a cross between a goat and a deer, or (according to רבי יוסי) its own creature of undecided status.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים: a כוי is the wild ram. Some say it is the animal that comes from a male goat and a female deer. רבי יוסי says: a כוי is a creature of its own, and the חכמים did not decide whether it is a wild species or a domesticated species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the argument between רב יהודה and רב נחמן matches an older argument among the תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא matches רב נחמן (wild ram). רבי יוסי matches רב יהודה (its own creature, never decided). The יש אומרים matches the view the גמרא used until now, that a כוי comes from a goat and a deer.

keyTerms.meaning: This matches an argument among the תנאים
Some say. Another opinion in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute among the Tannaim:
A koy is the wild ram,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַבָּא מִן הַתַּיִישׁ וּמִן הַצְּבִיָּיה.
phrases.english: It is the animal that comes from a male goat and a female deer.
Rabbi Yosei says:
A koy is a creature of its own,
and the Sages did not decide about it

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִין חַיָּה אִם מִין בְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: whether it is a wild species or a domesticated species.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the argument in Step 9 already appears among the תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the ברייתא, the כוי is a wild ram; or (יש אומרים) a cross between a goat and a deer; or (רבי יוסי) its own creature of undecided status.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the כוי is a domesticated animal
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a כוי is a בהמה. He shows this from the house of Dushai, who raised whole flocks of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: it is a kind of domesticated animal, and the house of Dushai used to raise many flocks of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with one more opinion, which gives a firm answer: a כוי is a בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי יוסי, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does decide the question. His evidence is practical: people kept כויים in flocks, the way people keep domesticated animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The house of Dushai, a family that raised these animals

steps.whatToRemember: There are several views of the כוי: a goat-deer cross, a wild ram, its own creature of undecided status (רב יהודה / רבי יוסי), or a בהמה (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
It is a species of domesticated animal,
and the members of the house of Dushai
would raise flocks and flocks of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִין בְּהֵמָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final opinion in the same ברייתא, which holds that the כוי is a בהמה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כוי is a בהמה, as shown by the flocks raised by the house of Dushai.

steps.title: Forest goats may be brought on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא (quoted through רב ספרא and רבי זירא) rules that forest goats are fit to be offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב ספרא, who said in the name of רב המנונא: these forest goats are fit to be brought on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling: wild-looking 'forest goats' may be brought as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a בהמה (a domestic animal) may be brought on the מזבח, never a חיה (a wild animal). So this ruling means רב המנונא holds that forest goats count as real goats, which are a בהמה. This connects to the earlier discussion about animals of unclear status, like the כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Forest goats, goats that live in the wild

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Safra said
that Rav Hamnuna said:
These forest goats
are fit to go up on the altar,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כוי to another animal of unclear status, the forest goat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forest goats are a kind of goat and may be offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: The reason: the Torah lists exactly ten kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא follows רבי יצחק, who says the תורה lists ten kosher animals and no more. Forest goats are not among the wild animals listed, so they must be goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יצחק, who said: the פסוק lists ten kosher animals and no more. Since forest goats are not counted among the wild animals, we learn that they are goats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב המנונא thinks forest goats are regular goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in דברים list three domestic animals and seven wild ones, and רבי יצחק says that list is complete. Forest goats are not one of the seven wild animals, so they cannot be a חיה. The only option left is that they are a kind of עז, a domestic goat.

phrases.english: He holds like this teaching
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: עֶשֶׂר בְּהֵמוֹת מָנָה הַכָּתוּב, וְתוּ לָא.
phrases.english: The verse counted ten animals, and no more.
phrases.notes: דברים 14:4–5. Three are domestic (ox, sheep, goat) and seven are wild.

phrases.english: And these, since it does not count them
together with the wild animals –
learn from this that they are goats.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning behind רב המנונא's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That forest goats are a kind of domestic goat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's rule that the list of ten kosher animals in דברים 14 is complete.

steps.title: Maybe the list of wild animals is not complete
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב argues that the list of wild animals is a פרט followed by a כלל ('any animal'). By the rule of פרט וכלל, the כלל adds more animals, so there could be other kosher wild animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב objected: Say instead that 'deer and gazelle' is a detail, and 'any animal' is a general statement. When a detail is followed by a general statement, the general statement adds to the detail, so there are many more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the list of ten is complete, which would knock out the proof that forest goats are goats.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the rules for reading the תורה says that when a list (פרט) is followed by a general phrase (כלל), the general phrase widens the list. The next פסוק says 'any animal that has split hooves', so other wild animals may be kosher too. If so, forest goats could be a wild animal that is simply not named, and then they could not go on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A detail followed by a general statement; the general statement widens the list

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge does not say forest goats are not kosher. The question is only whether they are a domestic goat (allowed on the מזבח) or an unnamed wild animal (not allowed).

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov objected to this:
But say that "deer and gazelle" is a detail,
and "any animal" is a general statement.
phrases.notes: This is from the next פסוק, דברים 14:6.

phrases.english: A detail followed by a general statement –
the general statement adds on to the detail,
so there are many more.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of step 13 that the list of ten is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that the פסוק lists ten kosher animals and no more.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the rule of פרט וכלל, 'any animal' widens the list, so forest goats could be an unlisted wild animal.

steps.title: Then why list so many animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the כלל were meant to widen the list, there would be no need to name so many wild animals. So the list is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need all these details?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יצחק's rule against the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה wanted to include every wild animal through the כלל, naming one would have been enough to set up a פרט וכלל. Naming seven shows the list is meant to be exact. So the proof that forest goats are goats stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Details, the items on the list

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need all these details?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא בר יעקב's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the challenge's reading makes part of the פסוק pointless.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general phrase 'any animal' widens the list, so there are more kosher wild animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The many details show the list is exact; there are only ten kosher animals.

steps.title: Maybe forest goats are the listed wild goat
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא asks: even if the list is complete, maybe forest goats are the אקו, the wild goat named on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא objected: But maybe they are a kind of אקו (wild goat)!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב המנונא's proof, from a different direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed forest goats are not on the list of wild animals. But one of the seven listed wild animals is the אקו, a wild goat. Forest goats might be that animal, which would make them a חיה, not fit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Wild goat, one of the seven wild animals in the list

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge accepts that the list is complete and still undercuts the proof, because forest goats might already be on the list as a wild animal.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, objected to this:
But maybe they are a kind of wild goat!
phrases.notes: The אקו is one of the seven wild animals listed in דברים 14:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the list is complete but attacks the assumption that forest goats are not on it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in step 13 that forest goats are not counted among the wild animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forest goats may be the אקו, a wild animal already on the list, so they would be a חיה.

steps.title: Maybe forest goats are a wild ox or a wild sheep
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא (or רב אחא בריה דרב אויא) suggests to רב אשי that forest goats may be a kind of תאו or זמר, which are wild animals on the תורה's list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי (some say it was רב אחא son of רב אויא): Maybe they are a type of wild ox or a type of wild sheep?
steps.whatsHappening: Another challenge is added to the last one. The list of wild animals may be complete, but forest goats might still be one of the other wild animals on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said forest goats might be the אקו. This step offers two more candidates from the same list: the תאו and the זמר. If forest goats are any of these, they are a חיה and cannot go on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild ox, one of the kosher wild animals listed in the תורה
A wild sheep, also on the list of kosher wild animals

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַוְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Acha son of Rav Avya who said to Rav Ashi:
Perhaps they are a type of wild ox
or a type of wild sheep?
phrases.notes: Both animals are named in the list of kosher wild animals in דברים 14:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא מִינָא דִּתְאוֹ אוֹ מִינָא דְּזֶמֶר נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more wild animals to the 'maybe it is the אקו' challenge of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that forest goats must be goats because they are not on the wild-animal list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forest goats may not need their own name on the list. They could simply be the תאו or the זמר that is already listed.

steps.title: אמימר permitted their fat
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן tells רב אשי that אמימר allowed eating the חלב of forest goats, which shows he treated them as a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said to רב אשי: אמימר permits their fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן reports what אמימר actually did with forest goats. This goes against רב המנונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלב of a בהמה is forbidden, but the חלב of a חיה is allowed. If אמימר let people eat the fat of forest goats, he held they are a חיה. That means they are not goats and could not be offered on the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Their fat (the forbidden kind of fat, חֵלֶב)
Certain fats that are forbidden in a בְּהֵמָה but allowed in a חַיָּה

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the challenges against רב המנונא are left unanswered, and אמימר is reported to treat forest goats as a חיה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan said to Rav Ashi:
Ameimar permits their fat.
phrases.notes: Fat like this is only allowed if the animal is wild, so אמימר must have seen them as wild animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר שָׁרֵי תַּרְבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the doubts of steps 16-17 with a real ruling that treats forest goats as wild animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that forest goats are fit for the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Permitting their חלב only makes sense if they are a חיה, and a חיה cannot be brought on the מזבח.

steps.title: A second version: can forest goats go on the altar?
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the discussion, אבא בריה דרב מנימין בר חייא asks רב הונא בר חייא whether forest goats may be offered on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא son of רב מנימין בר חייא asked רב הונא בר חייא: These forest goats, what is the law about offering them on the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the whole forest-goat discussion in a different way. This step is the question that opens it, and the answer comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question that רב המנונא ruled on in step 12, but it is now asked as a real question. The answer will be given with a different reason, based on a משנה and not on רבי יצחק's 'ten animals' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Forest goats, goats that live in the wild
For use on the מִזְבֵּחַ, meaning as a קָרְבָּן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is a second telling of the same discussion from step 12, with different people and a different reason.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מִנְיָמִין בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Abba son of Rav Minyamin bar Chiya asked
of Rav Huna bar Chiya:
These forest goats,
what is the law regarding the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second version of the discussion that began in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are forest goats a בהמה that may be offered as a קרבן?

steps.title: The only argument is about the wild ox
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא answers that רבי יוסי and the רבנן argue only about שור הבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי יוסי and רבנן only argue about the wild ox.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא starts his answer. He points to a known argument and says it covers only one animal, the שור הבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is setting up a contrast. The argument is limited to the wild ox, so there is no argument about forest goats. Steps 21-22 explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: They only argue as far as this, and no further

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis only disagree
about the wild ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The only argument is about שור הבר, so forest goats are not in doubt.

steps.title: The משנה about the wild ox and the reasons on each side
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says the רבנן hold שור הבר is a בהמה and רבי יוסי holds it is a חיה. The רבנן learn this from the תרגום, and רבי יוסי from its place on the list of wild animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: The wild ox is a type of domestic animal; רבי יוסי says it is a type of wild animal. רבנן hold that since we translate it as תורבלא (forest ox), it is a type of domestic animal. רבי יוסי holds that since it is counted with the wild animals, it is a type of wild animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that רב הונא בר חייא was talking about and explains each side's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן see that the תרגום calls the תאו a 'forest ox', so to them it is really an ox, which is a בהמה. רבי יוסי says the תורה put it on the list of wild animals, so it is a חיה. Both reasons depend on the animal being named in the תורה, and that matters for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Forest ox, the Aramaic translation of תְּאוֹ
Since we translate it (in the תַּרְגּוּם)

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
The wild ox is a type of domestic animal;
Rabbi Yosei says: a type of wild animal.
For the Rabbis hold:
since we translate it as 'torbala' (forest ox),
phrases.notes: The word being translated is תאו from דברים 14:5. The Aramaic calls it a 'forest ox'.

phrases.english: it is a type of domestic animal;
and Rabbi Yosei holds:
since the verse counts it together with the wild animals,
it is a type of wild animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the argument mentioned in step 20, with the reasons on both sides.
steps.raayaObject: That the argument is tied to the שור הבר being named on the wild-animal list
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כלאים about שור הבר, together with the תרגום of תאו

steps.title: Everyone agrees forest goats are goats
steps.stepSummary: Forest goats are not named among the wild animals, so all agree they are goats and may go on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these forest goats, everyone agrees they are a type of goat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא finishes his answer. Forest goats are ordinary goats according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי called the wild ox a חיה only because the תורה listed it with the wild animals. Forest goats are not on that list, so even רבי יוסי has no reason to call them wild. They count as goats and are fit for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of goat, a domestic animal

steps.whatToRemember: The second version reaches the same ruling as רב המנונא, that forest goats are goats and fit for the מזבח, but it builds it on the argument about שור הבר.

phrases.english: But these forest goats,
according to everyone, they are a type of goat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָנֵי דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 21 to finish the answer to step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Forest goats are goats according to all opinions and may be offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: Maybe forest goats are the wild goat
steps.stepSummary: In this second version too, רב אחא בריה דרב איקא challenges: maybe forest goats are the אקו, which is on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of Rav Ika objected: But maybe they are a type of wild goat!
steps.whatsHappening: The same challenge from the first version now comes back against the second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא's reason works only if forest goats are not on the list. But the list does include the אקו, a wild goat, and forest goats might be that animal. If so, רבי יוסי's reason would apply to them too.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild goat, one of the listed kosher wild animals

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same challenge as step 16. The גמרא repeats it here because it is aimed at the second version of the discussion.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika objected to this:
But perhaps they are a type of wild goat!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that forest goats are not on the wild-animal list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They may be the listed אקו, so רבי יוסי's reason could make them a חיה.

steps.title: Or maybe a wild ox or wild sheep
steps.stepSummary: רבינא suggests to רב אשי that forest goats may be a kind of תאו or זמר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But maybe they are a type of wild ox or a type of wild sheep!
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge is added in this version. It names two other wild animals from the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as step 17, now said by רבינא. Any of these listed wild animals could be what forest goats really are, so it is not clear that they are missing from the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Wild animal, which cannot be brought as a קָרְבָּן

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps they are a type of wild ox,
or a type of wild sheep!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מִינָא דְּתָאוֹ אוֹ מִינָא דְּזֶמֶר נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more possible wild animals to the challenge of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion in step 22 that forest goats are goats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forest goats might be the listed תאו or זמר, which would make them a חיה.

steps.title: אמימר permitted their fat, in this version too
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells רב אשי that אמימר permitted the חלב of forest goats, which treats them as a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב אשי: אמימר permits their fat.
steps.whatsHappening: The second version ends the same way as the first, with אמימר's ruling against calling forest goats ordinary goats. Here רב נחמן reports it instead of רב חנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permitting their חלב shows that אמימר held forest goats are a חיה. This goes against רב הונא בר חייא's claim that everyone agrees they are goats.

keyTerms.meaning: Fat of a domestic animal, which is forbidden
Fat of a wild animal, which is permitted
Fit to be offered on the altar

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions say forest goats are goats. In both, the reply is that they may be one of the listed wild animals, and that אמימר treated their fat as permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Ashi:
Ameimar permits their fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר שָׁרֵי תַּרְבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats step 18's report, now aimed at the second version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that everyone agrees forest goats are goats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר permitted their חלב, which shows he held they are a חיה, so not everyone agrees.

steps.title: The whole משנה is not like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה, and רבי אושעיא states that the entire משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'How so? One who slaughters, etc.' רבי אושעיא says: the whole משנה is not according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section on the משנה about אותו ואת בנו. רבי אושעיא makes a broad claim about whose opinion the whole משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a claim about authorship. רבי אושעיא says no part of this משנה fits רבי שמעון's view, so the משנה must follow other תנאים. The גמרא will now have to show what forces this conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה is about to explain the cases in detail

steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing which תנא a משנה follows shapes how we read every case in it, and possibly how we rule.

phrases.english: How so? One who slaughters, etc.
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה about slaughtering an animal and its child on the same day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Oshaya says:
The entire mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: כּוּלַּהּ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It moves from the forest-goats discussion to the next משנה about אותו ואת בנו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The entire משנה of כיצד השוחט does not follow רבי שמעון.

steps.title: How do we know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that the משנה is not like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אושעיא's claim. This is a setup line before the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא made a sweeping statement. Before accepting it, the גמרא wants to see which words in the משנה clash with רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: From where is this derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the proof behind רבי אושעיא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the משנה shows that it does not follow רבי שמעון?

steps.title: The case of קדשים slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: The proof starts from the משנה's case of two sacrificial animals, a mother and its child, slaughtered outside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From what the משנה teaches: if they were קדשים slaughtered outside, for the first one he is liable to כרת. Both animals are פסול, and for both he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the specific line in the משנה that it will use as proof. It quotes the case of קדשים slaughtered outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first slaughter outside brings כרת, the punishment for שחוטי חוץ, and the משנה gives lashes for both. For the second animal to bring lashes for אותו ואת בנו, the first slaughter must count as a real slaughter, even though it was done outside and its meat can never be eaten. Counting that first slaughter is what will clash with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrificial animals slaughtered outside the עזרה
Being cut off, a heavenly punishment

phrases.english: From that which the mishna teaches:
If they were sacrificial animals slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard,
for the first one, he is liable to karet,
and both animals are disqualified,
and for both of them, he receives the forty lashes.
phrases.notes: In practice the lashes are thirty-nine, but they are always called 'the forty'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָא תָנֵי: קָדָשִׁים בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'from where' by pointing to a specific case in the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that for קדשים slaughtered outside, both slaughterings bring lashes.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: an unfit slaughter is not a slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי שמעון's rule that a slaughter that cannot make the meat permitted is not called a slaughter. This sets up the clash with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, we have heard that רבי שמעון says: a slaughter that is not fit is not called a slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in רבי שמעון's general rule. It is setting up the next move: showing why the משנה's ruling cannot fit his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, if a slaughter cannot make the meat permitted to eat, it does not count as a halachic slaughter. קדשים slaughtered outside can never be eaten, so that slaughter is 'unfit'. The גמרא finishes connecting this to the lashes in the משנה on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, since (introduces a known fact for an argument)
A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted to eat
Is not called (does not count as) a slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not fit' here does not mean the knife or the cut was bad. It means the slaughter cannot make the meat permitted, like קדשים slaughtered outside.

phrases.english: After all, we have heard that Rabbi Shimon
says: a slaughter that is not fit
is not called a slaughter,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר: שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה – לֹא שְׁמָהּ שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the other half of the proof: רבי שמעון's principle, which will be set against the משנה's ruling from step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's known rule that שחיטה שאינה ראויה לא שמה שחיטה.
